page: Amazon Web Services c6in.16xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 64 virtual CPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor features a 54 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. This instance does not include local storage or GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core performance and Passmark CPU scores falling into the top 25% tier. The instance demonstrates strong performance in specialized tasks, including software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, and image processing. Cryptographic and extended instruction tests also rank in the top tier. However, single-core performance, memory bandwidth, and text processing benchmarks remain in the average tier.

The instance features a high baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps, which supports its strong static web serving throughput of 45.26 GB/sec. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high vCPU-to-RAM density and lack of bundled local storage make it a specialized resource optimized for network-heavy and compute-bound workloads rather than memory-intensive databases. Appropriate workloads include multi-threaded software compilation, image processing, static web serving, and medium-scale LLM text generation.
